alex: quick report: found a goroutine leak in the Go generator iterator when auth refresh races a context cancel. Repro is short.

rita: can you paste the minimal repro and logs?

alex: gist: calling iter.Next(ctx) while auth refresh (slow provider) triggers a detached retry goroutine. Canceling ctx returns from Next but the refresh goroutine keeps looping and logging.

sam: which API? pull-style iterator?

alex: yes. minimal snippet:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 800*time.Millisecond)
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
for iter.Next(ctx) { _ = iter.Token() }
// iter.Err() shows deadline, but goroutines keep running
```

alex: logs show repeated "auth: refresh start" after ctx deadline. workaround: wrap transport retry with select on ctx.Done() or pass ctx into auth refresh.

rita: short-term: add iter.Close() so callers can explicitly stop internal workers; long-term: make auth refresh cancellation-aware. I'll open an issue and update the sample app to show "defer iter.Close()".

ci-bot: created issue #2620: "go-sdk: iterator Close() + auth refresh cancellation" assigned to @rita.

sam: thanks for clear repro, alex. test suggestion: fake slow auth in CI and assert no goroutine growth after cancel.

alex: I'll PR a small sampleapp change and a flaky-resistant unit test.
